initialContact.message: Hi! I'm 25 and I've never had a credit card. My parents always said they're dangerous, so I've just used my debit card. But I'm thinking of buying an apartment in a few years and I've heard having a credit history helps. Should I get a credit card? And how do I use it without getting into trouble like my parents warned?

problemContext.currentSituation: Wants to build credit history, no previous credit experience, family fears about credit cards

idealAdvice: Validate parents' concern - credit cards CAN be dangerous if misused
In Finland, credit history is less important than in US, but still helpful
Get card with no annual fee and good benefits
Use it like debit card: only spend what you have
Pay full balance every month - never carry a balance
Set up automatic payment to avoid ever missing a payment
Start with low credit limit to minimize risk
Use for regular purchases (groceries, gas) and pay off immediately
This will build payment history without costing you anything
commonMistakes: Dismissing parents' concerns without acknowledging valid points
Not explaining that Finland's credit system differs from US
Recommending high credit limits for beginners
Not emphasizing paying full balance monthly
Making credit cards sound scary rather than empowering
Not discussing specific strategies to avoid debt

initialContact.message: Quick update - I got a credit card 6 months ago and it's been great! I use it for groceries and gas, and the automatic payment pays it off in full every month. I've never paid a cent in interest and I'm earning cashback. My parents are still skeptical, but I'm managing it well. I'm thinking of applying for a small loan to further build my credit. Good idea?

problemContext.currentSituation: Successfully using credit card responsibly, wants to optimize credit building

idealAdvice: DON'T take out a loan just to build credit - that's expensive and unnecessary
Continue current strategy - it's working perfectly
When you're ready to buy apartment, you'll have payment history
Focus on saving for down payment instead
6 months is good start, 1-2 years is even better
Your parents might come around when they see your responsibility
Credit building is a side benefit, not a goal in itself
commonMistakes: Agreeing that taking out unnecessary loan is good idea
Not celebrating the successful responsible use
Not emphasizing that saving for down payment is more important than credit score
